MARKETS — EVENING EDITION, SATURDAY 24 OCTOBER 2026. Read 19:41 BST.

*** THE HONEST POSITION: THIS TICKER IS ALMOST IDENTICAL TO OUR MORNING EDITION'S. ***
It is a Saturday night. Nine of the ten markets we track have been shut since Friday, so nine of
these ten figures are the SAME Friday closes we published at 11:33 this morning. The ONLY market
open is Bitcoin, and it is the only figure that has moved. This is stated plainly in the ticker
drivers rather than presented as a fresh set of readings.

THE ONE REAL MOVE SINCE THIS MORNING
  Bitcoin  80,436.82 (-0.95%) at 11:21  ->  80,244.43 (-1.19%) at 19:41
  A further fall of about $192, or 0.24 points of its daily percentage. Small, and the only thing
  the weekend has actually priced. No approved source attributes it and none is asserted.

CROSS-CHECKS
  Bitcoin  CNBC 80,244.43 (-1.19%)  vs  Trading Economics 80,245 (-1.02%)
           LEVELS AGREE to within 57 cents. The percentages differ by 0.17 points because the two
           providers measure a 24-hour window from different start points; the level is what we
           publish and the change is the primary feed's. Declared rather than reconciled.
  The nine closed markets were cross-checked this morning at 11:21 and those checks stand: the FTSE
  agreed to the penny across both providers, the gilt agreed on level, and the ten-year Treasury
  agreed on level and change at 5.00%.

DECLARATIONS CARRIED FORWARD FROM THIS MORNING, STILL TRUE TONIGHT
  1. Trading Economics' Brent page was $13.45 low this morning — the eleventh consecutive day it has
     been wrong by roughly $8 to $14. The oil level rests on the primary feed alone.
  2. The ten-year Treasury reads 4.999% on one feed and 5.00% on the other. NO CLAIM THAT IT HAS
     FALLEN BELOW 5% APPEARS ANYWHERE IN THIS EDITION, for the third consecutive day.
  3. The primary feed's previous-close field for the gilt has drifted repeatedly (5.3299 on Friday,
     5.3612 today), so the published day-move rests on our own Friday-afternoon reading.

TIMEZONE NOTE — LAST EDITION ON BST
  Checked at publication: tm_isdst = 1, zone = BST, UTC offset +1. The clocks go back at 02:00
  TOMORROW, 25 October. *** THIS IS THE LAST EDITION FOR WHICH apply_brief.py's HARDCODED
  offset = "+01:00" IS CORRECT. *** From tomorrow it must be +00:00 or every edition's market
  timestamp will be an hour wrong. Flagged to the editor; the script has not been altered.

NOTE ON THIS EDITION: no evening edition was produced by the scheduled job, which failed at its
sixth consecutive slot. Attempt one ran 18:09:38 to 18:16:30 and attempt two 19:17:22 to 19:17:32 —
seven minutes and then ten seconds, both exiting with code 1. The brevity, and an authentication
step the editor performed shortly afterwards, point to the runs dying before they began any work:
they wrote zero cache files and did not touch index.html.

*** THIRD AND FINAL READ, 19:55 BST, IMMEDIATELY BEFORE APPLYING ***
Bitcoin 80,307.40, -1.11% (previous read 19:41: 80,244.43, -1.19%).
It is the only market that can move tonight, and it moved again between the two reads — up $63 from
the 19:41 figure, leaving it $129 below this morning's 80,436.82 rather than the $192 recorded above.
THE PUBLISHED FIGURE IS 80,307 / -1.11, and four places were updated to match: the markets JSON, the
Bitcoin ticker driver, the sources block in the edition, and this note. The other nine figures are
Friday's closes and cannot have changed.
This is the same propagation discipline applied on 21 and 23 October: when a re-read supersedes a
figure, every place that cites it has to be corrected, not just the ticker.
